Source: A 25-year-old man is brought to the emergency department by paramedics for altered mental status.
His temperature is 98.0°F (36.7°C), blood pressure is 130/80 mmHg, pulse is 80/min, and respirations are 12/min with a saturation of 97% on room air.
The patient is easily arousable to voice and sternal rub but falls asleep rapidly.
He is able to state his name and knows that he is at the hospital and has an otherwise normal neurologic exam.
On arrival, the patient has slurred speech and is somnolent.
Physical exam reveals a sleeping man with miotic pupils.
Further is unable to be elicited.
He was found lying down at a bus stop unresponsive.
